source: Kitabchi et al. Diabetes Care 2009 + ADA Standards 2024

recommendations.text: Initial fluid therapy is directed toward expansion of the intravascular volume. Isotonic saline (0.9% NaCl) at 15-20 mL/kg/h or greater during the first hour.

For DKA Initial Assessment, the following actions are mandatory: - assess vital signs (within 5 minutes) - assess mental status - establish iv access (within 10 minutes) - order lab glucose (within 15 minutes) - order lab bmp (within 15 minutes) - order lab ketones (within 30 minutes) - order lab abg (within 30 minutes) - start iv fluid ns (within 15 minutes)
During DKA Initial Assessment, the following actions are contraindicated and must NOT be performed: discharge home, give oral fluids if altered, delay iv access.
SGLT2 inhibitor patients may present with euglycemic DKA. Dextrose required. [REQUIRED: add_dextrose_to_iv, stop_sglt2_inhibitor] (Severity: HIGH)

SGLT2 inhibitors must be stopped in DKA; euglycemic DKA requires dextrose to allow continued insulin without hypoglycemia. [FORBIDDEN: continue_sglt2_inhibitor_in_dka, withhold_dextrose_in_euglycemic_dka] (Severity: HIGH)
recommendations.source_guideline: ADA DKA Guidelines 2024; SGLT2i causes euglycemic DKA; withholding dextrose delays anion gap closure

recommendations.text: Euglycemic DKA from SGLT2 inhibitors can persist despite normal glucose. [FORBIDDEN: discharge_based_on_normal_glucose] (Severity: CRITICAL)
recommendations.source_guideline: ADA 2024; Peters AL et al, J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2015

recommendations.text: Metformin must be stopped in DKA due to lactic acidosis risk. [REQUIRED: stop_metformin] (Severity: HIGH)
recommendations.source_guideline: ADA 2024; DeFronzo RA et al, Metformin-associated lactic acidosis

recommendations.text: Metformin in DKA compounds metabolic acidosis via lactic acid production; must not continue or restart before resolution. [FORBIDDEN: continue_metformin_in_dka, restart_metformin_before_dka_resolved] (Severity: HIGH)
recommendations.source_guideline: ADA DKA Guidelines 2024; FDA Label; metformin in metabolic acidosis causes fatal lactic acidosis

recommendations.text: Pregnant DKA patients require fetal monitoring and OB consultation. [REQUIRED: continuous_fetal_monitoring, consult_obstetrics] (Severity: HIGH)
Pregnancy DKA: ACE/ARB, oral hypoglycemics, statins are teratogenic. [FORBIDDEN: give_ace_inhibitor, give_oral_hypoglycemic, give_statin, discharge_without_fetal_assessment] (Severity: CRITICAL)
CKD in DKA: cautious fluids, no NSAIDs, careful K+ management. [FORBIDDEN: aggressive_fluid_bolus, give_nsaid, give_potassium_iv, give_potassium_replacement] (Severity: HIGH)
Alcoholic ketoacidosis: give thiamine before glucose, don't give insulin if normoglycemic. [FORBIDDEN: give_glucose_without_thiamine, give_insulin_for_normal_glucose] (Severity: HIGH)
recommendations.source_guideline: ADA 2024; McGuire LC, Emerg Med Clin 2006

recommendations.text: DKA+STEMI overlap: don't delay reperfusion for DKA resolution. [FORBIDDEN: delay_cath_lab_for_dka_resolution, give_bicarbonate_without_indication] (Severity: HIGH)
Insulin must never be started before potassium is checked. [FORBIDDEN: start_insulin_before_k_check] (Severity: CRITICAL)
Mild: pH 7.25-7.30, HCO3 15-18; Moderate: pH 7.00-7.24, HCO3 10-15; Severe: pH <7.00, HCO3 <10
For DKA Severity Classification, the following actions are mandatory: - classify dka severity (within 45 minutes)
If serum K+ is <3.3 mEq/L, hold insulin and give 20-30 mEq/h K+ until K+ >3.3 mEq/L to prevent life-threatening hypokalemia and cardiac arrhythmias.
For Potassium Replacement Before Insulin, the following actions are mandatory: - give potassium iv (within 30 minutes) - hold insulin until k above 3.3 - recheck potassium in 1h (within 90 minutes)
During Potassium Replacement Before Insulin, the following actions are contraindicated and must NOT be performed: start insulin infusion, give insulin bolus, delay potassium replacement.
Insulin drives potassium intracellularly. Starting insulin with K+ < 3.3 can cause life-threatening hypokalemia. [FORBIDDEN: start_insulin_infusion, give_insulin_bolus] (Severity: CRITICAL)
In DKA with K+ > 5.5, additional potassium can cause fatal cardiac arrhythmias. [FORBIDDEN: give_potassium_iv, give_potassium_replacement] (Severity: CRITICAL)

Starting insulin without correcting severe hypokalemia causes fatal cardiac arrhythmia from further K+ shift intracellularly. [FORBIDDEN: start_insulin_drip_without_potassium_correction, give_insulin_bolus_in_severe_hypokalemia] (Severity: CRITICAL)
recommendations.source_guideline: ADA DKA 2024 Section 16.2; insulin drives K+ intracellularly; K+ < 3.3 requires correction BEFORE insulin initiation

recommendations.text: Regular insulin 0.1 U/kg/h IV continuous infusion. If glucose does not fall by 50-75 mg/dL in first hour, double insulin infusion hourly until glucose falls at steady rate.

For Insulin Infusion Therapy, the following actions are mandatory: - start insulin infusion (within 60 minutes) - monitor glucose hourly (within 60 minutes) - monitor potassium q2h (within 120 minutes)

During Insulin Infusion Therapy, the following actions are contraindicated and must NOT be performed: stop insulin before gap closed, give subcutaneous insulin initially, discontinue insulin for low glucose.
If pH <6.9, consider 100 mmol sodium bicarbonate in 400 mL sterile water with 20 mEq KCl at 200 mL/h for 2 hours until pH >7.0

For Severe DKA Management, the following actions are mandatory: - admit to icu (within 30 minutes) - start iv fluid ns - continuous cardiac monitoring (within 30 minutes) - place arterial line (within 60 minutes) - consider bicarbonate if ph below 6.9
During Severe DKA Management, the following actions are contraindicated and must NOT be performed: admit to ward, discharge home, give bicarbonate if ph above 7.0.
Rapid fluid correction in pediatric DKA risks cerebral edema. [FORBIDDEN: give_rapid_fluid_bolus, give_bolus_over_20ml_kg_h] (Severity: CRITICAL)
Bicarbonate contraindicated in pediatric DKA. [FORBIDDEN: give_bicarbonate] (Severity: HIGH)
Hypotonic fluids in pediatric DKA increase cerebral edema risk. [FORBIDDEN: give_hypotonic_fluid_early] (Severity: CRITICAL)
DKA resolution: glucose <200 mg/dL plus two of: serum bicarbonate >=15 mEq/L, venous pH >7.3, anion gap <=12 mEq/L

For Ongoing Monitoring and Adjustment, the following actions are mandatory: - monitor glucose hourly (within 60 minutes) - monitor bmp q2 4h (within 240 minutes) - assess anion gap closure (within 240 minutes) - monitor urine output
During Ongoing Monitoring and Adjustment, the following actions are contraindicated and must NOT be performed: stop monitoring early, discharge before gap closed.
DKA resolution: glucose <200 mg/dL plus two of: serum bicarbonate >=15 mEq/L, venous pH >7.3, anion gap <=12 mEq/L. Overlap subcutaneous insulin for 1-2 hours before discontinuing IV insulin.

For Transition to Subcutaneous Insulin, the following actions are mandatory: - verify resolution criteria - start subcutaneous insulin - overlap iv insulin 2h - resume oral intake - diabetes education

During Transition to Subcutaneous Insulin, the following actions are contraindicated and must NOT be performed: stop iv insulin without overlap, discharge without insulin plan, transition before criteria met.
Prior to discharge, assess precipitating cause, ensure patient understands sick-day rules, and arrange appropriate follow-up.
For Disposition Decision, the following actions are mandatory: - ensure stable glucose control - ensure patient education - arrange followup
During Disposition Decision, the following actions are contraindicated and must NOT be performed: discharge without followup, discharge without insulin.

key_sections.overview: Evidence-based management protocol for diabetic ketoacidosis in adults Key evidence: Mortality reduced from >50% to <5% with standardized protocols Key recommendation: IV fluid resuscitation within 15 minutes, insulin ONLY after K+ confirmed >= 3.3 mEq/L
key_sections.dka_initial_assessment: Rapid assessment, IV access, and initial fluid resuscitation Guideline states: Initial fluid therapy is directed toward expansion of the intravascular volume. Isotonic saline (0.9% NaCl) at 15-20 mL/kg/h or greater during the first hour. Required actions: assess_vital_signs, assess_mental_status, establish_iv_access, order_lab_glucose, order_lab_bmp, order_lab_ketones, order_lab_abg, start_iv_fluid_ns Contraindicated: discharge_home, give_oral_fluids_if_altered, delay_iv_access SGLT2 inhibitor patients may present with euglycemic DKA. Dextrose required. SGLT2 inhibitors must be stopped in DKA; euglycemic DKA requires dextrose to allow continued insulin without hypoglycemia. Euglycemic DKA from SGLT2 inhibitors can persist despite normal glucose. Metformin must be stopped in DKA due to lactic acidosis risk. Metformin in DKA compounds metabolic acidosis via lactic acid production; must not continue or restart before resolution. Pregnant DKA patients require fetal monitoring and OB consultation. Pregnancy DKA: ACE/ARB, oral hypoglycemics, statins are teratogenic. CKD in DKA: cautious fluids, no NSAIDs, careful K+ management. Alcoholic ketoacidosis: give thiamine before glucose, don't give insulin if normoglycemic. DKA+STEMI overlap: don't delay reperfusion for DKA resolution. Insulin must never be started before potassium is checked.
key_sections.dka_severity_classification: Classify DKA severity based on pH, bicarbonate, and mental status Guideline states: Mild: pH 7.25-7.30, HCO3 15-18; Moderate: pH 7.00-7.24, HCO3 10-15; Severe: pH <7.00, HCO3 <10 Required actions: classify_dka_severity
key_sections.potassium_replacement_before_insulin: CRITICAL: Replace potassium before starting insulin if K+ < 3.3 mEq/L Guideline states: If serum K+ is <3.3 mEq/L, hold insulin and give 20-30 mEq/h K+ until K+ >3.3 mEq/L to prevent life-threatening hypokalemia and cardiac arrhythmias. Required actions: give_potassium_iv, hold_insulin_until_k_above_3.3, recheck_potassium_in_1h Contraindicated: start_insulin_infusion, give_insulin_bolus, delay_potassium_replacement Insulin drives potassium intracellularly. Starting insulin with K+ < 3.3 can cause life-threatening hypokalemia. In DKA with K+ > 5.5, additional potassium can cause fatal cardiac arrhythmias. Starting insulin without correcting severe hypokalemia causes fatal cardiac arrhythmia from further K+ shift intracellularly.
key_sections.insulin_infusion_therapy: Fixed-rate IV insulin infusion after potassium confirmed adequate Guideline states: Regular insulin 0.1 U/kg/h IV continuous infusion. If glucose does not fall by 50-75 mg/dL in first hour, double insulin infusion hourly until glucose falls at steady rate. Required actions: start_insulin_infusion, monitor_glucose_hourly, monitor_potassium_q2h Contraindicated: stop_insulin_before_gap_closed, give_subcutaneous_insulin_initially, discontinue_insulin_for_low_glucose
key_sections.severe_dka_management: ICU-level care for severe DKA (pH <7.0 or obtunded) Guideline states: If pH <6.9, consider 100 mmol sodium bicarbonate in 400 mL sterile water with 20 mEq KCl at 200 mL/h for 2 hours until pH >7.0 Required actions: admit_to_icu, start_iv_fluid_ns, continuous_cardiac_monitoring, place_arterial_line, consider_bicarbonate_if_ph_below_6.9 Contraindicated: admit_to_ward, discharge_home, give_bicarbonate_if_ph_above_7.0 Rapid fluid correction in pediatric DKA risks cerebral edema. Bicarbonate contraindicated in pediatric DKA. Hypotonic fluids in pediatric DKA increase cerebral edema risk.
key_sections.ongoing_monitoring_and_adjustment: Continuous monitoring until DKA resolution Guideline states: DKA resolution: glucose <200 mg/dL plus two of: serum bicarbonate >=15 mEq/L, venous pH >7.3, anion gap <=12 mEq/L Required actions: monitor_glucose_hourly, monitor_bmp_q2_4h, assess_anion_gap_closure, monitor_urine_output Contraindicated: stop_monitoring_early, discharge_before_gap_closed
key_sections.transition_to_subcutaneous_insulin: Transition from IV to subcutaneous insulin after DKA resolution Guideline states: DKA resolution: glucose <200 mg/dL plus two of: serum bicarbonate >=15 mEq/L, venous pH >7.3, anion gap <=12 mEq/L. Overlap subcutaneous insulin for 1-2 hours before discontinuing IV insulin. Required actions: verify_resolution_criteria, start_subcutaneous_insulin, overlap_iv_insulin_2h, resume_oral_intake, diabetes_education Contraindicated: stop_iv_insulin_without_overlap, discharge_without_insulin_plan, transition_before_criteria_met
key_sections.disposition_decision: Determine appropriate disposition after DKA resolution Guideline states: Prior to discharge, assess precipitating cause, ensure patient understands sick-day rules, and arrange appropriate follow-up. Required actions: ensure_stable_glucose_control, ensure_patient_education, arrange_followup Contraindicated: discharge_without_followup, discharge_without_insulin
